tracks.text: I'm Jonathan Kershaw. I build demonstrations that help people see what technology can make possible. The journey begins with a familiar problem: a room full of powerful ideas, and no shared picture of what changes for the business. My work connects those worlds. I turn a technical mechanism into a story people can enter, question, and use. Across Red Hat platforms, applied AI, and partner ecosystems, the goal is the same: make the next decision clearer. Welcome to Cognitive Overdrive. Let's move from possibility to something you can inspect.

Every journey has a call to action. Mine starts by understanding the room. An executive needs to connect a capability to a business decision. A solution architect needs to see the boundaries, dependencies, and tradeoffs. Sales needs a story the customer recognizes. Internal teams need something they can deliver again. I design those entry points around one technical foundation. Choose an audience here, and the emphasis changes with it. The craft is knowing what to reveal, when to reveal it, and which evidence helps this person move forward.

The work takes different forms because the audience needs different ways in. The Great CPU Bake Off turns a placement decision into a memorable business story. Edge Inference at Scale connects constrained compute to a human need. AERIS explores a cinematic inspection scenario, clearly labeled as a concept. Triforce brings the depth: multi-agent workflows, tools, event contracts, and heterogeneous compute. The platform story is Red Hat aligned. Intel reference work, recorded AMD runs, historical NVIDIA fleet evidence, and Arm portability each have their own qualification boundary. Different stories, one discipline: make the mechanism clear, show what the evidence supports, and give the audience a useful next step.

Now cross the threshold into the system. A diagram should answer a question. Trace the request, reveal the boundary, then explain why that component exists. In Triforce, Python, Java, and Go connect business workflows through tools, routing, and event-driven coordination. In the Praxis lab, application teams use a stable gateway contract while the platform controls backend choices. Red Hat OpenShift provides a common platform context across this work. Hardware portability becomes a design discipline: preserve the application contract, qualify each target, and show the evidence for the path actually being discussed.

A convincing demonstration should survive a difficult question. What happens when the evidence is missing? What if permission is withdrawn? This chapter lets you test that idea in a browser simulation. No model or backend is running here. Change a condition and watch the decision respond. The purpose is to make the rule understandable, including the point where the system must stop. The wider portfolio separates source implementations, recorded results, and rehearsal candidates. That clarity gives an architect something to inspect, and a business leader a sound basis for the next conversation.

The reward is a capability that travels beyond one presenter. Launchpad is central to that ambition. Its documented pilot brings catalog intake, individual labs, workshops, qualification checks, and environment cleanup into a shared delivery experience. Participants get a place to learn. Instructors get a repeatable workshop. Content teams get a path to contribute. The same principle shapes my sovereign AI, virtualization, and agentic learning tracks: connect a concise story to architecture, a separate hands-on lab, and an evidence-aware handoff. One investment can support executive conversations, sales discovery, technical depth, and internal enablement.

The journey returns to the audience with something useful: a clearer decision, an inspectable system, and a path to take the work forward. That is what I bring as a demo engineer. Storytelling and technical leadership meet in the same experience. Motion gives the idea shape. Architecture explains the mechanism. Evidence earns confidence. Reusable delivery helps the organization carry it further. This portfolio is an invitation to explore that craft together. Choose a real customer problem, and let's walk through how I would turn it into an experience that makes the next step clear.
